correctness.rationale: Exponential-time Brownian displacement has MGF M(s)=1/((1-as)(1+bs)). The two-sided Poisson construction at a deterministic observation time gives Y=xi+C Y' in law with independent terms; the backward expansion converges in L² by the triangle inequality and E[C²]<1. Synchronously coupled starting values contract almost surely, because for some rho<1 marks C<=rho occur infinitely often. For necessity, the MGF of C Y' equals (1-as)^(1-p)(1+bs)^(1-r) on (-1/b,1/a); if either shape is below one, this would tend to zero at the corresponding finite endpoint, impossible by Fatou's lemma applied to the positive exponentials. Deconvolution gives gamma shapes (p-1,r-1) for C Y', interpreting zero shape as a point mass. If just one shape is one, the deconvolved law is nonzero but one-sided, inconsistent with nonnegative C and the two-sided Y'; if both are one it forces C=0. With both shapes greater than one there is no atom at zero, so C preserves sign. Gamma-ratio sign probabilities reduce to the beta CDFs at x=b/(a+b); differentiating the displayed difference in (3) and checking its zero endpoint verifies the identity for all real p,r>1. Its only interior zero forces b(p-1)=a(r-1). For sufficiency use H(s)=theta*integral_0^1 t^(theta-1)V(ts) dt for both signs of s (equivalently the printed s^(-theta) expression for positive s). Then sH'=theta(V-H); the proposed deconvolved MGF satisfies this with H(0)=1 by direct differentiation, and power series determine each coefficient since theta+k>0. The transforms therefore solve the fixed point. Finally the even moment ratios determine the law of C² on [0,1], hence C. This is an analytic audit for all real shapes in scope, not an inference from the frozen finite moment checker, which was inspected but not run.

For a Poisson shot-noise process with decay e^(-t), rate theta and innovation xi, backward interarrival decay factors have Beta(theta,1) law. The bilateral exponential xi is a mixture of signed exponentials with probabilities a/(a+b) and b/(a+b); Poisson splitting gives the deconvolved stationary gamma shapes theta*a/(a+b) and theta*b/(a+b).
